explain: A request handler validates input and returns a stable task identity instead of exposing provider internals. This ordinary function models an HTTP boundary without starting a server.
steps: Receive a decoded request body. || Return a validation error or an accepted task with a status location.
name: http-lifecycle

explain: Approval binds exact owner, parameters, revision, and expiry. Changing the request invalidates the stored approval before a business write.
steps: Record a reviewed payload and its validity. || Compare the current request with that payload using trusted server state.
name: business-confirmation

explain: A committed record and a derived projection can temporarily disagree. Compare revisions before presenting the projection as current.
steps: Update the authoritative task revision. || Detect that the search/UI projection has not caught up and expose pending synchronization.
name: projection-lag

explain: Correlation connects a request to its worker and tool calls across component boundaries. These dictionaries model trace relationships without exporting telemetry.
steps: Assign a common trace identity and explicit parent span IDs. || Check that the worker and retrieval spans belong to the same tree.
name: trace-tree

explain: A browser submits JSON, checks HTTP status, validates the result shape, and treats transport failure separately. Abort support lets the caller stop obsolete waiting.
steps: Await fetch and explicitly inspect response.ok. || Parse the body only after HTTP success and reject an invalid task identity.
expect: With a compatible local API: a task object; HTTP errors or invalid data reject the promise.
limit: Browser integration sketch; it requires your API at /tasks and is syntax-checked, not a live provider or server test.
name: browser-fetch

explain: A dictionary indexes tasks by identity; a deque represents pending work; a set prevents duplicate scheduling. Their different roles are explicit.
steps: Build lookup, membership, and queue structures from the same task identity. || Dequeue work and look up its record directly.
name: structures

explain: Translate internal runtime events into a small public schema. Private framework fields stay inside the adapter.
steps: Read only allowlisted internal fields. || Emit the stable public task and text fields consumed by the frontend.
name: adapter-events

explain: Working session state and durable messages have different lifetimes. A small retained history is rehydrated from persisted records.
steps: Keep a durable ordered message fixture. || Create a bounded working window for the current session rather than treating every past message as active context.
name: session-vs-record

explain: A knowledge fact describes policy; a procedure constrains an action. The dispatcher requires an authorized confirmation even when the fact is available.
steps: Separate the read-only policy from the action requirements. || Evaluate the action predicate independently from the answer text.
name: procedure-vs-fact

explain: An executable threat-model fixture pairs entry points with protected assets and controls. Coverage checks expose a boundary that has no stated enforcement.
steps: List the controls required at each entry. || Assert that all external entry points have at least one named control.
name: trust-map
authoritative-service-boundary-guard
explain: An authoritative service boundary harness demonstrates why placing authorization in the HTTP/chat controller layer creates cross-tenant data leaks in background workers, and validates mandatory security context enforcement at the domain service layer.
steps: Demonstrate that controller-level authorization protects chat routes while leaving background worker tasks vulnerable. || Enforce mandatory security context passing at the domain service boundary. || Verify that background workers cannot bypass tenant isolation rules.
expect: All authoritative service boundary guard invariants verified successfully.
